source: Native AWS SDK for Go v2; isolated throwaway module/executable; ListBackups only

experiment.nativeEndpointOverridePolicy: Removed all AWS_ENDPOINT_URL* environment entries; AWS_IGNORE_CONFIGURED_ENDPOINT_URLS=true; explicitly set native regional BaseEndpoint

phases.name: greedy
phases.sequential: Issue next SDK call immediately after prior call returns; no explicit pacing or retries

experimentDetails.credentialHandling: SDK default credential chain; no credentials logged; account checked by existing DynamoDBProbe/aws_cli helper and again by SDK before first ListBackups.
experimentDetails.tableFilterPurpose: Unique absent table name; no table or backup created; successful responses all contain empty BackupSummaries.

rateDefinitions.offeredRequestsPerSecond: Actual HTTP RoundTrip starts divided by elapsed seconds from first HTTP start through final response body completion, separately for each phase. Not scheduled target rate.
rateDefinitions.acceptedRequestsPerSecond: Success responses divided by the same elapsed time.
rateDefinitions.requestStartToStartRate: (N-1) divided by last-minus-first actual HTTP RoundTrip start time; avoids the short-phase N/span endpoint-count effect.
rateDefinitions.oneSecondBins: Actual HTTP start and body-complete times in half-open one-second bins relative to each phase first HTTP start; accepted/rejected allocated by completion. Final bin may be partial.
rateDefinitions.tenSecondBinsByRequestStart: Greedy request outcomes grouped by actual HTTP starts in half-open ten-second bins. Final completion occurs 0.034542237 seconds after the 120-second start window.

analysis.conclusion: This one persistent native us-east-1 HTTP/1.1 connection exposed a sustained accepted rate consistent with the published ListBackups 5 requests/second limit: 604 successes and 496 native throttles from 1100 actual attempts in 120.034542237 seconds. After the initial 10-second bin (54 successes), each of the next eleven 10-second bins had 50 successful requests. Actual offered rate 9.164028782882557/s exceeded 5/s, so network latency did not prevent measurement.
limitations: One connection, one account, one region, one 120-second sequential phase; no quota, shard-count, token-capacity, refill-clock, or routing algorithm inferred.
The initial 54 successes per ten-second bin do not establish burst capacity. Sustained behavior is observable; exact allowance scope and burst model remain unresolved.

The earlier 64-connection phase ran at another time and much greater offered load. This is not a synchronized controlled experiment isolating connection count; no claim that allowance is literally per TCP connection or can be multiplied by connection count.

Possible cross-operation background traffic: Main reported that the independent bootstrap probe was issuing Create/Describe/Restore operations in us-east-1 during this work. This experiment did not observe or measure overlap with those calls and does not assume account-wide isolation. Main withheld its own ListBackups calls until these phases finished.
This read-only probe created no table or backup and did not test CreateBackup or other operation admission.
No second regional endpoint needed: this connection achieved more than five actual HTTP starts per second.
Recovery proves all paced requests succeeded, not an exact refill or recovery-time threshold.

Request.GetBody was nil; serialized request bytes were not captured. Empty requestBody placeholders were removed. Supplied SDK inputs and native HTTP target headers remain available; response body/header evidence is unaffected.

comparison.interpretation: Single-connection greedy acceptance was approximately 5/s with 45.09% rejection, unlike 164.23/s aggregate acceptance and 9.60% rejection in the prior 64-connection phase. Both returned HTTP 400 modeled ThrottlingException with com.amazon.coral.availability namespace, and both paced recoveries succeeded. The single-connection result is consistent with documented sustained rate but does not explain the prior aggregate allowance.

cleanup.verification: Owned /tmp directory removed after successful process exit; pathlib.exists false for directory, source and executable. No AWS resource creation/mutation calls were made, therefore no AWS delete calls or resource absence claims are necessary.

scopedSharingFollowup.purpose: Single-connection ListBackups sharing across table filters, mixed ListBackups/DescribeBackup admission, and invalid-input throttle precedence

experiment.baseline: Initial experiment supplies baseline; this scoped follow-up begins directly with alternating filters.
experiment.retryer: aws.NopRetryer; exactly one actual HTTP attempt per call observed
experiment.nativeEndpointPolicy: Remove all AWS_ENDPOINT_URL* overrides; AWS_IGNORE_CONFIGURED_ENDPOINT_URLS=true; explicit native STS and DynamoDB BaseEndpoint; no proxy.
experiment.recovery: Four valid ListBackups calls after two-second idle, one-second sleep between completed calls.
experiment.sdkVersions: Same isolated Go module dependency versions as the initial experiment; copied current repository go.mod/go.sum to /tmp, built with -mod=readonly; no repository manifest changes.
experiment.rateDefinitions: Offered = actual HTTP attempts / first HTTP start through last response-body completion; success and nonThrottled use same denominator. NonThrottled includes native validation/not-found errors and is not synonym for success. Per-input subgroup rates share the whole-phase denominator. Single preflight N/span is latency reciprocal, not a sustained load measurement.

interpretation.tableFilters: Two alternating nonexistent filters each offered below 5/s (4.5148/s and 4.4981/s) nevertheless both received throttles; combined acceptance 5.0312/s over 60.0250s. This supports sharing across these two filters on this persistent connection, not an independent five-per-second allowance per TableName.
interpretation.operationMix: Alternating ListBackups/DescribeBackup produced 8.6710 nonthrottled responses/s in aggregate: ListBackups 4.3438 successes/s plus DescribeBackup 4.3272 BackupNotFoundException/s. No throttles observed. This does not behave like one shared five-per-second gate counting both observed request paths. It is consistent with operation-specific admission, but the missing-backup path might bypass or differently consume DescribeBackup admission; this experiment does not prove independent budgets for all valid requests.
interpretation.invalidInput: The SDK sent Limit=0 (one actual attempt), and preflight received native ValidationException. Sustained identical invalid calls offered 9.2026/s yielded 304 ValidationException and 249 ThrottlingException in 60.0919s; after initial ten-second bin, each next bin had exactly 50 validation responses. Native throttling can therefore take precedence over the Limit=0 constraint error; invalid requests are not categorically rejected before all admission checks. No generalized ordering across other invalid fields or operations is inferred.
interpretation.recovery: Sequences 1618–1621 returned Success after the invalid-input phase and two-second idle; this does not establish exact recovery/refill timing.

limitations: Single connection/account/region, sequential fixed-order phases, unique nonexistent table filters and missing backup only. No shard count, token capacity, refill model, or account-global allowance inferred.

Bootstrap sibling may issue Create/Describe/Restore operations in us-east-1 concurrently; actual overlap was not measured. Account-wide traffic isolation is not assumed. Main reported its short ListBackups measurement finished before this follow-up, with no further ListBackups planned.

DescribeBackup request rate was below its documented 10/s limit, and ListBackups rate during the mixed phase was below its documented 5/s; the mixed phase tests a shared 5/s explanation, not the full DescribeBackup admission boundary.

Serialized request bytes were unavailable because Go Request.GetBody was nil. Exact SDK input structs, actual HTTP targets, and complete native response bodies/headers remain retained; this limitation also applies to the initial experiment and is now explicit there.

documentation.observedStatement: You can call ListBackups a maximum of five times per second; Limit minimum 1, maximum 100.
You can call DescribeBackup at a maximum rate of 10 times per second.

encoding.offsetUnit: integer nanoseconds from originUTC; no rounding
encoding.normalization: Every native response body/header preserved; Date and X-Amzn-Requestid stored per row; remaining response headers deduplicated exactly in Go net/http canonical form. SDK error request ID replaced with {requestId}, reversible from row. Request targets/URLs and exact SDK input structs deduplicated. Timing/result rows not sampled.
encoding.requestHeaderSampling: Raw examples alone retain noncredential allowlist Content-Type, X-Amz-Target, Amz-Sdk-Request, Amz-Sdk-Invocation-Id, User-Agent. Credential-bearing headers never recorded.
encoding.rawExampleSelection: First call of each (phase,responseVariant,requestVariant), every fresh connection, final call of each phase, every SDK rejection without HTTP.
encoding.zeroAttemptRows: HTTP/connection/response fields null; complete SDK error and input preserved as raw example.
encoding.requestBodyCaptureLimitation: Request.GetBody was nil for every Go SDK HTTP request, so serialized request-body bytes were not captured. Empty placeholder strings have been removed, not represented as empty wire bodies. requestVariants.sdkInput preserves supplied Go SDK structs; their null/empty optional fields are struct serialization, not a claim those fields were sent on wire. Native response bodies and HTTP target headers were captured.
